about: Announced datacenters and the defaults /impact offers a datacenter from them (docs/methods/forecast.md, the datacenter sections). Each row is one named project and one public document, every figure with the document's words. The defaults are medians over the rows that state both figures, each with its count, lowest and highest; a reader changes any of them. The MW of the rows measure different things (IT capacity, critical IT, critical grid capacity, power required), kept in each row; construction jobs are headcounts as announced (at peak where the document says so), never job-years.
source: warehouse/forecast/datacenter_announced_rows.json, transcribed by chain 740 (lab-desktop window 3) from the documents named in each row, read 2026-11-26 (runs/c740/probe/probe.csv requests on lab-desktop)
dollars: 2025 dollars by the GDP implicit price deflator of deflator.json; a 2026 announcement is taken as 2025 dollars

mw_stated.name: MW as stated
mw_stated.how: the MW each document states, whatever it measures (IT capacity, critical IT, critical grid capacity, power required)

investment_per_mw.name: Investment per MW
investment_per_mw.how: investment over the MW the document states; rows whose investment includes power plants left out

permanent_jobs_per_mw.name: Permanent jobs per MW
permanent_jobs_per_mw.how: permanent or operational jobs over the MW stated; jobs of a kind not stated left out

permanent_jobs_per_billion.name: Permanent jobs per billion dollars
permanent_jobs_per_billion.how: permanent or operational jobs over the investment

construction_jobs_per_billion.name: Construction jobs per billion dollars
construction_jobs_per_billion.unit: construction jobs (headcount as announced) per USD billion (2025)
construction_jobs_per_billion.how: construction jobs as announced over the investment; at peak or period not stated, as each row says
